claims.text: The challenge() method inverts the original condition - original guard was context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(), but new guard isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) is true only when user != null, so users who submit bad username will see error page without WebAuthn form
The new override method shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is missing the @Override annotation, unlike its sibling overrides in the same file.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.
PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest has an unused import of PasswordCredentialModel that is never referenced anywhere in the file.
PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest is left with an orphaned unused import of NoSuchElementException after this PR removed the two assertThrows(NoSuchElementException...) call sites that used it.

To share the constant used above, it was widened from protected to public and the authenticators.util package now imports from authenticators.browser, which itself already imports from util, creating a bidirectional dependency between the two packages.

The test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey actually tests 'passkeys disabled for the realm', not 'user has no passkey' as its name and comment claim; the realm-enabled-but-user-has-no-passkey combination that this PR newly opens up is left untested.

The USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note now has two separate places that independently read and interpret it — AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError duplicates logic already present in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth — so a future change to how it's interpreted has to be made in two places.

Two test assertions use a try/findElement/fail()/catch(Exception) pattern to assert an element doesn't exist, which swallows any unrelated WebDriver exception as a false pass, instead of using the project's existing assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) convention.

Whether WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator is considered an extensible API outside this repository, since making shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators always return false changes fillContextForm's null-return behavior in a way external extenders might depend on.

Whether re-authentication triggers other than prompt=login (e.g. max_age, required actions, account console re-auth) also flow through the same UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate path with an already-set user, since only prompt=login is covered by the new tests.
Same element absence check issue at lines 312-317 - try/catch pattern should be replaced with Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)

findElement throws NoSuchElementException when element doesn't exist (doesn't return null), and catching generic Exception is too broad - should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) instead
Catch `NoSuchElementException` instead of `Exception` so unexpected Selenium/runtime failures do not get treated as successful assertions

Now that re-authentication knows exactly who the user is, the passkey conditional UI is still shown purely based on realm-level policy without checking whether that specific user actually has a passwordless WebAuthn credential, so a user without one gets a passkey button that is guaranteed to fail.

The new shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators extension point has an undocumented implicit precondition — any override returning true must guarantee context.getUser() is non-null, or WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean's constructor will NPE — and the javadoc doesn't state this.
